news.headline: Trump Threatens to Cut Off Trade Unless the Fed Cuts Rates — the Fed Has Not Cut Rates
news.summary: トランプ大統領は、連邦準備制度が利下げを行わなければ貿易赤字を抱える国々との取引を停止すると脅迫した。FRBは金利を据え置いたままだ。

commentary: 矛盾: 連邦準備制度は法律上の独立機関なのに、大統領が「利下げしなければ貿易をやめる」と脅している。脅迫先は外国ではなく、自国の中央銀行なんですよ。
滑稽さ: 雇用統計が好調すぎて、FRBは逆に利上げを検討し始めた。「下げろ」と叫んだら「上げる話が出てきた」。
日本・海外から見ると: 外交上の脅しを国内の金融政策にも使い始めたのか、と各国の中央銀行関係者は静かに眉をひそめているはずです。
imagePrompts: A president figure at a podium pointing an accusing finger at a large stone building labeled 'Federal Reserve,' while the building's windows show people inside simply drinking coffee and ignoring him
A split scoreboard: left side reads 'Trump: Cut Rates,' right side reads 'Jobs Report: Maybe Raise Rates,' with a bewildered referee in the middle
A man shouting into a phone labeled 'Trade Threat' while the call display reads 'Recipient: The Fed — Status: Unmoved'
captions: He threatened foreign countries to pressure a domestic agency that is literally designed to be unpressurable. Bold strategy.
The jobs report came in hot, the Fed started eyeing rate hikes — and somewhere Trump is still posting about cuts.
You want the Fed to listen? They've got one job and 'listening to the president' isn't on the list.
Tariffs against Canada because the Fed won't budge. Canada's just standing there like, 'We don't set your interest rates?'
The Fed's response: silence. The jobs report's response: maybe a hike. The market's response: yields up. Sir, this is going great.
captionsJa: 自国の独立機関を動かすために外国を脅す。すごい迂回路ですね。
雇用統計が強すぎて、FRBは利上げ方向。「下げろ」と叫んだ週に、これ。
FRBに一個だけ仕事がある。「大統領の言うことを聞く」は入ってないんですよ。
カナダへの関税でFRBを動かそうとしてる。カナダ「えっ、私たちアメリカの金利決めてないんですけど」。
FRBの反応：沈黙。雇用統計の反応：利上げ示唆。市場の反応：金利上昇。まあ順調じゃないですか。
candidates.newsEn: President Trump doubled down on threats to halt trade with countries where the U.S. runs deficits unless the Federal Reserve lowers interest rates. The Fed, which operates independently of the White House, has not indicated any plans to cut rates. Trump made the demands via social media posts on Friday. Treasury yields rose following a strong jobs report, suggesting the Fed may actually hike rates.

ironyEn.contradiction: The president threatened other countries to pressure an institution he legally cannot control. It's like leaving a strongly worded note for your landlord — addressed to your neighbor.
ironyEn.absurdity: Trump demanded rate cuts the same week a blowout jobs report made rate hikes more likely. The economy trolled him back.
ironyEn.outside: Central banks worldwide spent decades building independence from politicians. The U.S. president is now negotiating tariffs to undermine his own.

ironyEn.contradiction: The Fed's whole job is to ignore exactly this kind of pressure. Trump found the one institution in Washington that is structurally required to not care what he says.
ironyEn.absurdity: The threat is essentially: 'Cut rates or Canada suffers.' Canada has not yet weighed in on U.S. monetary policy.
ironyEn.outside: Foreign finance ministers watching this are taking notes — not on how to negotiate, but on what not to do.

news.headline: Federal Bureau of Prisons Signs Exclusive Deal to Sell Prisoners Unapproved Nicotine Pouches
news.summary: 連邦刑務所局（BOP）が、FDA未承認のニコチンパウチを受刑者に独占販売するフロリダのスタートアップと排他的契約を締結していたことが明らかになった。

commentary: 矛盾: 受刑者を「社会から隔離して保護する」はずの機関が、FDA未承認品の独占販売ルートを刑務所内に開いた。受刑者は消費者として断れない立場なんですよ。
滑稽さ: 「captive customer（囚われた顧客）」という言葉がこんなに字義通りに使われたことが、ビジネス史上あったでしょうか。
日本・海外から見ると: 民間企業が刑務所内で独占商売できる構造、日本では考えにくい。アメリカの「官民連携」の射程の広さに改めて驚く。
imagePrompts: A prison commissary window with a single brand of nicotine pouches prominently displayed, a long line of inmates in front of it, and a 'Exclusively Available Here' banner overhead
A startup founder in a business suit shaking hands with a prison warden in front of a building with iron bars, both grinning, a 'No FDA Approval Required' sticker on the product box between them
A flowchart showing: 'FDA Review' crossed out with a red X, arrow pointing to 'BOP Exclusive Contract,' arrow pointing to 'Captive Market,' arrow pointing to 'Profit'
captions: The feds found a customer base that literally can't walk out. Startup guys call this 'product-market fit.'
FDA approval? We've got a contract. Same thing, right?
A monopoly, an unapproved product, and zero exit options for the consumer — someone pitched this in a business school and got an A.
Most startups spend years searching for a captive audience. The BOP just handed one over.
The inmates can't leave, can't choose another brand, and can't return it. Five stars on the investor deck, though.
captionsJa: 逃げられない顧客層。スタートアップ界隈ではこれを「完璧なPMF」と呼ぶ。
FDA承認？　契約書がある。同じようなものでしょ。
独占、未承認、購買者に選択肢なし。MBAの授業でケーススタディにしたらA評価案件。
普通のスタートアップはキャプティブな顧客を探すのに何年もかかる。BOPが一発で解決してくれた。
受刑者は逃げられないし、他のブランドも選べないし、返品もできない。投資家へのピッチデックには最高のスライドができた。
candidates.newsEn: The Bureau of Prisons entered an exclusive arrangement in July with a Florida-based startup to sell nicotine pouches to federal prisoners. The pouches have not been authorized by the FDA. The deal gives a single company monopoly access to a captive customer base of federal inmates. The arrangement is now facing congressional scrutiny.

ironyEn.contradiction: The institution responsible for inmate welfare handed a monopoly on unregulated nicotine products to a startup — in a setting where customers literally cannot shop elsewhere.
ironyEn.absurdity: The FDA exists to decide what goes into Americans' bodies. The BOP decided: not our problem, exclusive deal signed.
ironyEn.outside: In most countries, a government agency selling unapproved substances to people in its own custody would be a scandal. Here it's a procurement contract.

ironyEn.contradiction: Prisons restrict what inmates can consume for safety reasons, then carve out an exclusive lane for an unvetted product.
ironyEn.absurdity: A Florida startup now has a monopoly customer base that cannot leave, complain to a competitor, or file a Yelp review.
ironyEn.outside: This is the most literal example of a captive market in the history of capitalism.

news.headline: The White House Released Arcade Games. Some Are Racist and Possibly Copyright Infringement.
news.summary: ホワイトハウスが政策PRのためのアーケードゲームシリーズを公開したが、一部は人種差別的な内容を含み、実在するゲームの著作権を侵害している可能性があると指摘されている。

commentary: 矛盾: 「法の支配」を掲げる行政府が、他社の著作物を無断使用した可能性のあるゲームでPRをしている。知的財産保護は他国に要求するやつですよね。
滑稽さ: テトリスのブロックを国境の壁に見立てるという発想、ゲームデザイナーが思いついていたとしても普通は止める。誰も止めなかったのが今回。
日本・海外から見ると: 「ビルド・ザ・ウォール」テトリスに対してテトリス社が声明を出す2026年。テトリスの生みの親はソ連出身のパジトノフさんです、念のため。
imagePrompts: An arcade cabinet in the White House lobby with the presidential seal on it, a politician in a suit playing it, and a lawyer from 'The Tetris Company' standing behind him holding a cease-and-desist letter
A row of retro arcade machines in a government hallway, each labeled with a policy name, with a copyright lawyer placing sticky notes on all of them
A Tetris-style game where the falling blocks are bricks labeled 'Wall' stacking up at a border, with a Soviet-era Tetris logo watermark visibly in the corner
captions: The White House made arcade games. The Tetris Company made a phone call.
Nothing says 'rule of law' like an IP lawsuit from a game invented in the USSR.
They could've just done a press release. They chose racist Tetris. Respect the commitment.
An official government communication that also might be copyright infringement — name a more Washington combo.
The Tetris Company is now a political actor. We're in the timeline.
captionsJa: ホワイトハウスがアーケードゲームを作った。テトリス社が電話した。
「法の支配」を掲げる政権に対して、ソ連生まれのゲームの会社が著作権警告。筋がいい。
プレスリリースで済んだはずなのに、人種差別的テトリスを選んだ。その信念は評価する。
政府の公式広報が同時に著作権侵害の疑いあり。ワシントンらしいコンボ。
テトリス社が政治プレイヤーになる世界線に来てしまった。
candidates.newsEn: The White House released a series of policy-themed arcade games for public relations purposes. Several of the games have been criticized as racist, and some appear to be based on existing commercial games whose copyright holders have not given permission. The Tetris Company has already responded publicly to a game called 'Build the Wall,' which appears to mimic its product.

ironyEn.contradiction: An administration that routinely threatens other countries over IP theft apparently didn't clear the rights on its own PR games.
ironyEn.absurdity: Someone in the White House thought Tetris blocks stacking into a border wall was a good idea and then nobody in the room said 'wait.'
ironyEn.outside: The Tetris Company — a game invented in the Soviet Union — is now issuing legal warnings to the U.S. government. The Cold War has entered its final form.

ironyEn.contradiction: The government that signs executive orders to protect American IP launched a campaign that may infringe on someone else's IP.
ironyEn.absurdity: These are official White House communications. The official communications are racist arcade games. This sentence is real.
ironyEn.outside: Foreign governments trying to understand U.S. policy now have the option of playing an arcade game. Diplomatic briefings have not historically included a joystick.

news.headline: Coroner Confirms Measles Killed a 6-Week-Old. RFK Jr. Had Disputed the Deaths.
news.summary: ペンシルベニア州ランカスター郡の検死官が、生後6週間の乳児の死因がはしかであると確認した。RFKジュニアはこれより前、同郡でのはしか関連死を公式に否定していた。

commentary: 矛盾: 国民の健康を守る省のトップが、自国の検死官が確認した死因を事前に否定していた。「信頼できる情報源」が省内にいるんですが。
滑稽さ: ワクチンで防げたはずの病気で乳児が亡くなった週に、保健長官はその死を「ゲーム」と表現された行為で疑っていた。
日本・海外から見ると: はしかは日本でも2019年に大流行が問題になった。ワクチンで封じ込められていたはずの感染症が、先進国で乳児の命を奪っている現実に、公衆衛生の専門家は言葉を失う。
imagePrompts: A government official standing at a podium labeled 'HHS' holding a sign reading 'I Dispute This,' while behind him a county coroner's office window displays an official death certificate marked 'Cause: Measles'
A timeline graphic on a wall: '2000 — Measles Eliminated in U.S.' with a celebratory stamp, then '2026 — Coroner Confirms Infant Death,' the second entry scrawled in red
An empty vaccination appointment card labeled 'MMR — Due at 12 Months' next to a newspaper headline about a 6-week-old measles death, on a hospital waiting room chair
captions: The coroner confirmed the cause of death. The HHS secretary had already decided not to believe that kind of information.
Six weeks old. MMR doesn't start until 12 months. Do the math — then stop, because the math is terrible.
Measles was eliminated in the U.S. in 2000. 'Was' is doing a lot of work in that sentence.
The data was inside his own department. He disputed it anyway. Bold move from the head of public health.
Other countries spent decades earning 'measles-free' status. We're watching one country hand it back.
captionsJa: 検死官が死因を確認した。保健長官はその種の情報を信じないと決めていた。
生後6週間。MMRワクチンは生後12ヶ月から。計算してみると、ひどい話になる。
はしかは2000年にアメリカで「根絶」された。「された」が重い。
データは自分の省の中にあった。それでも否定した。保健長官として大胆な選択。
他の国々が何十年もかけて「はしか排除」の認定を取った。返上している国をリアルタイムで見ている。
candidates.newsEn: The Lancaster County coroner in Pennsylvania confirmed that a 6-week-old infant died from measles. The death comes amid a growing outbreak in the county, which has already seen two measles-related deaths. Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who leads the Department of Health and Human Services, had publicly disputed measles-related death counts before the coroner's determination was announced.

ironyEn.contradiction: The head of the agency responsible for U.S. public health disputed measles deaths that a county coroner then officially confirmed. The coroner's job is literally to determine cause of death.
ironyEn.absurdity: A 6-week-old can't be vaccinated — the MMR shot comes at 12 months. The only protection available to that infant was the immunity of the people around them.
ironyEn.outside: Measles was declared eliminated in the U.S. in 2000. The word 'eliminated' is doing less work than it used to.

ironyEn.contradiction: RFK Jr. disputed measles deaths while running the department that tracks measles deaths. The data was already inside the building.
ironyEn.absurdity: The infant was too young for the vaccine. The disease won because enough adults around them weren't vaccinated. The HHS secretary disputes this chain of events.
ironyEn.outside: Countries that fought hard to achieve measles elimination status are watching the U.S. lose it in real time.

news.headline: Trump Will Fly to Ireland on Qatar's Gifted Jet — Security Questions Unresolved
news.summary: トランプ大統領が来週のアイルランド訪問に、カタールから贈与された航空機を使用する予定であることが明らかになった。7月の使用時にはイランの脅威情報が発覚し、大統領が別機に移送されるという事態が起きていた。

commentary: 矛盾: 前回使おうとしたらイランの脅威が発覚して乗り換えた飛行機を、セキュリティ問題が解決されないまま今度こそ国際便に使う。「学習」の概念はどこへ。
滑稽さ: アメリカ大統領専用機が外国から「もらいもの」で、しかし前回は脅威情報で降りることになったという事実。エアフォースワンのブランドイメージが泣いている。
日本・海外から見ると: 外国政府からの高額贈与品を大統領機にするという話、日本の公務員倫理規程的に考えると別次元の話。受け取れる金額の上限が「飛行機一機」ではない。
imagePrompts: A large jet with a Qatar Airways-style livery partially repainted with American flag motifs, sitting on a tarmac with a security official holding a clipboard labeled 'Unresolved Questions' standing under the wing
A president figure boarding a plane while a security aide holds up a yellow sticky note reading 'Same jet as July — issue not fixed,' the president waving without looking back
A gift box the size of an airplane with a bow on top and a tag reading 'From: Qatar. To: USA. Note: security features TBD'
captions: They pulled him off this plane in July over a threat. September fix: fly it to Europe.
The American president's ride to Ireland is a loaner from Qatar. The handshake photo's going to be something.
Security questions: unresolved. Departure date: next week. Someone in the Secret Service is not sleeping.
Most world leaders fly their own country's plane. Most.
It was risky in July. Same plane. It's September now — fine, I guess?
captionsJa: 7月にこの飛行機から降ろされた。9月の解決策：ヨーロッパへ飛ぶ。
アイルランドへ向かうアメリカ大統領の乗り物は、カタールからの借り物。握手の写真が楽しみ。
安全上の懸念：未解決。出発日：来週。シークレットサービスの誰かは今夜眠れない。
自国の飛行機で飛ぶ首脳がほとんど。ほとんど、ね。
7月はリスクありと判断された。同じ飛行機。9月になったから——まあいいか、という論理。
candidates.newsEn: President Trump plans to use a Boeing jet gifted by Qatar for his upcoming trip to Ireland, the first time the aircraft will be flown overseas since a July incident in which Trump was moved to a separate plane after officials learned of a possible Iranian threat to the Qatari jet. Security questions about the aircraft's defenses remain unanswered. The trip marks the plane's first international use since that incident.

ironyEn.contradiction: The last time Trump tried to use this jet, they pulled him off it mid-situation due to a threat. The security questions are still open. Next stop: Ireland.
ironyEn.absurdity: The presidential aircraft — symbol of American power — is a foreign gift with unresolved defensive capabilities. Air Force One is now an analogy.
ironyEn.outside: Most countries' ethics laws set gift limits for public officials somewhere below 'a Boeing jet.' The U.S. is operating in uncharted territory.

ironyEn.contradiction: The plane was deemed risky enough to evacuate the president from in July. The solution in September is to fly it to Europe.
ironyEn.absurdity: Qatar gave the U.S. a plane. The plane had a threat incident. The president is taking it to Ireland. Nobody is explaining the gap between step two and step three.
ironyEn.outside: Foreign leaders landing in their capital's airport to greet the American president will now be greeting a man who arrived on Qatar's plane. The optics of that handshake are doing a lot of work.

editorial.thread: 今日の5本を貫く糸は「ルールを決める側がルールを守らない」。FRBの独立性、FDA承認、著作権、公衆衛生のデータ、外交贈賄——それぞれ違う棚にある話だけど、全部そこに戻ってくる。
editorial.titleEn: The Rule-Makers Had a Very Busy Friday Breaking Rules
editorial.subtitleEn: Five stories, one theme, zero irony detected from inside the building.
editorial.titleJa: 「ルールを守れ」と言う人たちが今週やったこと、全部読んだ
titleAltJa: FRBを「脅す」、刑務所で未承認品を売る、著作権侵害ゲームを公開する——これが一週間の出来事です
『ビルド・ザ・ウォール』テトリスと生後6週間の話を、明日の飲み会で使える形にした
editorial.leadJa:
今日のニュース5本、開く前から少し憂鬱でした。

で、開いたら案の定でした。ただ、今日は「悪い話」というより「説明のつかない話」が多くて、それはそれで別の疲れ方をする。
editorial.introEn:
Five stories landed in my feed this morning and I had to put my phone down for a second.

Not because they were shocking. Because they all had the same shape: someone who writes the rules decided the rules were for other people. The Fed's independent — so threaten it anyway. FDA approval exists — sell without it anyway. Copyright law is real — remix it anyway. A coroner confirmed a cause of death — dispute it anyway. One plane caused a security evacuation in July — fly it internationally in September.

Here's your forecast: if you've ever followed a rule nobody else seemed to care about, today's news is your vindication. The system isn't broken because you failed to game it. It's just apparently optional at a certain altitude.

You've been playing fair. That turns out to be the interesting choice.
editorial.introJa:
「決める側が守らない」週があります。

今日の5本、並べてみたらそういう週でした。

FRBに「言うことを聞かなければ貿易をやめる」と脅した話。刑務所の中でFDA未承認のニコチンパウチを独占販売した話。ホワイトハウスが著作権侵害かもしれないゲームでPRをした話。7月にイランの脅威で降りた飛行機を、セキュリティ未解決のままアイルランドに飛ばす話。

あと、はしかで生後6週間の赤ちゃんが亡くなった話があります。これだけ笑えない。でも今日どうしても外せなかった。

今日の占いです。

「ちゃんとやってるのに、なんで自分だけ」——そう思うことがあるとしたら。今日のニュースを読むと、少し気が楽になるかもしれない。守らなかった人たちが今週これだけ新聞に載った。

あなたが守ってた分は、ちゃんとある。たぶん。
editorial.quipEn: This week, the U.S. government threatened its own central bank, sold unapproved products to people who can't say no, plagiarized a Soviet-era puzzle game, disputed a coroner's report, and booked a security-flagged plane for round two. Rules, it turns out, are vibes.
editorial.quipJa: 今週のアメリカ、自国の中央銀行を脅して、刑務所でFDA未承認品を売って、ソ連生まれのパズルゲームをパクって、検死官の報告を否定して、7月に降ろされた飛行機をもう一回飛ばそうとしています。ルールは気分らしい。
notesEn: Trump threatened to cut off trade with other countries unless the Federal Reserve cuts interest rates. The Fed is legally independent. Also, after a strong jobs report came in, the Fed started eyeing rate hikes. He asked for down, the data moved up, and the threat just kind of hangs there.

The Bureau of Prisons signed an exclusive deal to sell FDA-unapproved nicotine pouches inside federal prisons. The startup gets monopoly access. The customers are federally incarcerated and cannot leave. Business school calls this 'product-market fit.' I call it something else.

The White House released arcade games as a PR move. Some are racist. At least one appears to lift directly from Tetris — specifically a game called 'Build the Wall.' The Tetris Company, whose founder fled the Soviet Union, has responded. The irony is doing a lot of heavy lifting today.

A Lancaster County coroner confirmed a 6-week-old died from measles. Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who runs the Department of Health and Human Services, had publicly disputed measles death counts before this confirmation. The coroner didn't update his findings to match the secretary's opinion.

Trump is flying to Ireland on the Boeing jet gifted by Qatar — the same plane he was moved off of in July after officials learned of a possible Iranian threat. Security questions are still unresolved. The departure is next week. Someone is deciding this is fine.
xJa: 「FRBが利下げしなければ貿易を止める」とトランプ大統領が脅した。脅迫先は外国ではなく、自国の中央銀行です。で、その後に出た雇用統計が好調すぎて、FRBは逆に利上げを検討し始めた。「下げろ」と叫んだら「上がる話が出てきた」週。
連邦刑務所局が、FDA未承認のニコチンパウチをフロリダのスタートアップに独占販売させる契約を結んでいた。顧客は受刑者なので物理的に断れない。「キャプティブ（囚われた）顧客」という言葉がこれほど字義通りに使われた事例は少ないと思う。
ホワイトハウスがPR用のアーケードゲームを公開した。一部が人種差別的で、著作権侵害の疑いもある。「ビルド・ザ・ウォール」というテトリス風ゲームに対して、テトリス社がすでに反応した。テトリスの生みの親はソ連出身のパジトノフさんです。
ペンシルベニア州の検死官が、生後6週間の乳児の死因がはしかだったと確認した。RFKジュニアはこれより前、同地域のはしか関連死を公式に否定していた。検死官は長官の見解に合わせて報告書を変えなかった。
トランプ大統領が来週のアイルランド訪問に、カタールから贈られた飛行機を使う。7月にイランの脅威情報が発覚して大統領が別機に移送されたやつです。セキュリティ上の問題は未解決のまま。出発は来週。
raidEn: The Fed was designed specifically to not respond to this kind of pressure. Someone knew that when they built it. Apparently that's the detail that keeps getting missed.
"Captive customer base" has never been more literal. Someone in that pitch meeting had to know exactly what they were saying.
The Tetris Company issuing a statement to the White House is a sentence I didn't have on my 2026 bingo card. The USSR angle makes it poetry.
Six weeks old. MMR doesn't start until 12 months. There's nothing funny in this one — just the math, sitting there.
The fact that this is the same plane, and the security questions are still open, and the departure is next week — someone is very calm about this and I'd love to know why.
raidJa: 「FRBを脅す」という発想がすごくて、FRBはそもそも大統領の指示を聞かないように設計された機関なんですよね。その設計の話を記事で読んで、なんか複雑な気持ちになりました。
「キャプティブ（囚われた）顧客」という言葉がこんなにそのまま使われたビジネス事例、なかなかないですよね……と思いながら読みました。記事、とても丁寧にまとめられていました。

# The Rule-Makers Had a Very Busy Friday Breaking Rules

## Today's Forecast

Five stories landed in my feed this morning and I had to put my phone down for a second.

Not because they were shocking. Because they all had the same shape: someone who writes the rules decided the rules were for other people. The Fed's independent — so threaten it anyway. FDA approval exists — sell without it anyway. Copyright law is real — remix it anyway. A coroner confirmed a cause of death — dispute it anyway. One plane caused a security evacuation in July — fly it internationally in September.

Here's your forecast: if you've ever followed a rule nobody else seemed to care about, today's news is your vindication. The system isn't broken because you failed to game it. It's just apparently optional at a certain altitude.

You've been playing fair. That turns out to be the interesting choice.

---

## 1. Trump Threatens to Cut Off Trade Unless the Fed Cuts Rates — the Fed Has Not Cut Rates

*CNBC Top News — [source](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/04/trump-fed-rates-jobs-trade.html)*

President Trump doubled down on threats to halt trade with countries where the U.S. runs deficits unless the Federal Reserve lowers interest rates. The Fed, which operates independently of the White House, has not indicated any plans to cut rates. Trump made the demands via social media posts on Friday. Treasury yields rose following a strong jobs report, suggesting the Fed may actually hike rates.

**Why It's Funny**

Trump threatened to cut trade with deficit countries unless the Fed cuts interest rates. Here's the thing: the Fed is legally independent. Threatening it is like yelling at a vending machine to give you a discount — it's technically directed at something, but the machine doesn't have feelings or congressional oversight. Then the jobs report dropped, strong, and the Fed started talking about hiking rates. He said down. The economy said up. The threat is still out there, kind of floating.

**Say It Out Loud**

> He threatened foreign countries to pressure a domestic agency that is literally designed to be unpressurable. Bold strategy.

---

## 2. Federal Bureau of Prisons Signs Exclusive Deal to Sell Prisoners Unapproved Nicotine Pouches

*CBS News US — [source](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/bureau-prisons-nicotine-pouches-prisoners/)*

The Bureau of Prisons entered an exclusive arrangement in July with a Florida-based startup to sell nicotine pouches to federal prisoners. The pouches have not been authorized by the FDA. The deal gives a single company monopoly access to a captive customer base of federal inmates. The arrangement is now facing congressional scrutiny.

**Why It's Funny**

The Bureau of Prisons found a startup willing to sell nicotine pouches inside federal prisons exclusively — pouches the FDA hasn't approved. The customers are people who are federally incarcerated. They can't switch brands. They can't walk out. In venture capital this is called 'product-market fit.' In most other contexts it's called something that takes longer to say in polite company.

**Say It Out Loud**

> The feds found a customer base that literally can't walk out. Startup guys call this 'product-market fit.'

---

## 3. The White House Released Arcade Games. Some Are Racist and Possibly Copyright Infringement.

*The Verge — [source](https://www.theverge.com/policy/990520/trump-arcade-games-maga-copyright)*

The White House released a series of policy-themed arcade games for public relations purposes. Several of the games have been criticized as racist, and some appear to be based on existing commercial games whose copyright holders have not given permission. The Tetris Company has already responded publicly to a game called 'Build the Wall,' which appears to mimic its product.

**Why It's Funny**

The White House launched arcade games for PR. Couple of problems: some are racist, and at least one appears to be a Tetris clone called 'Build the Wall.' The Tetris Company has issued a public response. Worth knowing: Tetris was invented by Alexey Pajitnov, a Soviet computer scientist. The White House used a game from the USSR to promote its border policy, without permission, and someone had to make a phone call about it.

**Say It Out Loud**

> The White House made arcade games. The Tetris Company made a phone call.

---

## 4. Coroner Confirms Measles Killed a 6-Week-Old. RFK Jr. Had Disputed the Deaths.

*Ars Technica — [source](https://arstechnica.com/health/2026/09/measles-killed-6-week-old-baby-coroner-confirms-after-rfk-jr-disputed-deaths/)*

The Lancaster County coroner in Pennsylvania confirmed that a 6-week-old infant died from measles. The death comes amid a growing outbreak in the county, which has already seen two measles-related deaths. Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who leads the Department of Health and Human Services, had publicly disputed measles-related death counts before the coroner's determination was announced.

**Why It's Funny**

A Pennsylvania coroner confirmed a 6-week-old infant died from measles. Robert F. Kennedy Jr. — the man currently running the Department of Health and Human Services — had disputed measles death counts in that county before the coroner's finding came out. The coroner did not revise the cause of death. Measles was declared eliminated in the U.S. in 2000. That word is doing a lot of work right now.

**Say It Out Loud**

> The coroner confirmed the cause of death. The HHS secretary had already decided not to believe that kind of information.

---

## 5. Trump Will Fly to Ireland on Qatar's Gifted Jet — Security Questions Unresolved

*The Guardian US — [source](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/04/trump-qatar-jet-ireland)*

President Trump plans to use a Boeing jet gifted by Qatar for his upcoming trip to Ireland, the first time the aircraft will be flown overseas since a July incident in which Trump was moved to a separate plane after officials learned of a possible Iranian threat to the Qatari jet. Security questions about the aircraft's defenses remain unanswered. The trip marks the plane's first international use since that incident.

**Why It's Funny**

Trump is using the Qatar-gifted Boeing for his Ireland trip next week. This is the same plane he was pulled off of in July when officials learned of a possible Iranian threat. Security vulnerabilities: still unresolved, per reporting. Departure: next week. The logic here seems to be that if nothing bad happened last time — and something did happen last time — it probably won't happen this time.

**Say It Out Loud**

> They pulled him off this plane in July over a threat. September fix: fly it to Europe.

---

## Today's Punchline

> This week, the U.S. government threatened its own central bank, sold unapproved products to people who can't say no, plagiarized a Soviet-era puzzle game, disputed a coroner's report, and booked a security-flagged plane for round two. Rules, it turns out, are vibes.

# 「ルールを守れ」と言う人たちが今週やったこと、全部読んだ

## 今日を占うよ〜

「決める側が守らない」週があります。

今日の5本、並べてみたらそういう週でした。

FRBに「言うことを聞かなければ貿易をやめる」と脅した話。刑務所の中でFDA未承認のニコチンパウチを独占販売した話。ホワイトハウスが著作権侵害かもしれないゲームでPRをした話。7月にイランの脅威で降りた飛行機を、セキュリティ未解決のままアイルランドに飛ばす話。

あと、はしかで生後6週間の赤ちゃんが亡くなった話があります。これだけ笑えない。でも今日どうしても外せなかった。

今日の占いです。

「ちゃんとやってるのに、なんで自分だけ」——そう思うことがあるとしたら。今日のニュースを読むと、少し気が楽になるかもしれない。守らなかった人たちが今週これだけ新聞に載った。

あなたが守ってた分は、ちゃんとある。たぶん。

---

## 1. Trump Threatens to Cut Off Trade Unless the Fed Cuts Rates — the Fed Has Not Cut Rates

*CNBC Top News（[記事](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/04/trump-fed-rates-jobs-trade.html)）*

トランプ大統領は、連邦準備制度が利下げを行わなければ貿易赤字を抱える国々との取引を停止すると脅迫した。FRBは金利を据え置いたままだ。

**どこが笑える？**

トランプ大統領が「FRBが利下げをしなければ赤字国との貿易を止める」と投稿した。ここで一点確認なんですが、FRBは法律上の独立機関です。大統領の指示に従わないように設計されている機関に向かって「言うことを聞け」と脅す。脅迫先を間違えている、というより、脅迫の概念を拡張している。で、その後に出た雇用統計が好調すぎて、FRBは逆に利上げを考え始めた。「下げろ」と言ったら「上げる話が出てきた」。

これを脅しと呼んでいいのか、ただのすれ違いなのか。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> 自国の独立機関を動かすために外国を脅す。すごい迂回路ですね。

---

## 2. Federal Bureau of Prisons Signs Exclusive Deal to Sell Prisoners Unapproved Nicotine Pouches

*CBS News US（[記事](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/bureau-prisons-nicotine-pouches-prisoners/)）*

連邦刑務所局（BOP）が、FDA未承認のニコチンパウチを受刑者に独占販売するフロリダのスタートアップと排他的契約を締結していたことが明らかになった。

**どこが笑える？**

連邦刑務所局が、フロリダのスタートアップにFDA未承認のニコチンパウチを刑務所内で独占販売させる契約を結んでいた。顧客は受刑者なので、外に出て別の店で買うことができない。スタートアップ用語で「プロダクト・マーケット・フィット」という言葉があって、要は「その商品をどうしても必要とする人たちに売れている状態」のことなんですが。これがその言葉をいちばん文字通りに実現した事例かもしれない。

あと、FDA未承認です。念のため。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> 逃げられない顧客層。スタートアップ界隈ではこれを「完璧なPMF」と呼ぶ。

---

## 3. The White House Released Arcade Games. Some Are Racist and Possibly Copyright Infringement.

*The Verge（[記事](https://www.theverge.com/policy/990520/trump-arcade-games-maga-copyright)）*

ホワイトハウスが政策PRのためのアーケードゲームシリーズを公開したが、一部は人種差別的な内容を含み、実在するゲームの著作権を侵害している可能性があると指摘されている。

**どこが笑える？**

ホワイトハウスが政策PRのためのアーケードゲームを公開した。一部が人種差別的で、著作権侵害の疑いもある。「ビルド・ザ・ウォール」というゲームはどう見てもテトリスで、テトリス社がすでに声明を出した。ここで補足ですが、テトリスの生みの親はソ連のコンピューター科学者アレクセイ・パジトノフさんです。アメリカの国境政策をPRするために、ソ連生まれのゲームを無断で使った。テトリス社から電話がかかってきた。

止める人、いなかったのかな。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> ホワイトハウスがアーケードゲームを作った。テトリス社が電話した。

---

## 4. Coroner Confirms Measles Killed a 6-Week-Old. RFK Jr. Had Disputed the Deaths.

*Ars Technica（[記事](https://arstechnica.com/health/2026/09/measles-killed-6-week-old-baby-coroner-confirms-after-rfk-jr-disputed-deaths/)）*

ペンシルベニア州ランカスター郡の検死官が、生後6週間の乳児の死因がはしかであると確認した。RFKジュニアはこれより前、同郡でのはしか関連死を公式に否定していた。

**どこが笑える？**

ペンシルベニア州ランカスター郡の検死官が、生後6週間の乳児の死因がはしかだったと確認した。アメリカで保健福祉省のトップを務めるRFKジュニアは、この発表より前に、同郡でのはしか関連死を公式に否定していた。検死官は見解を変えなかった。

はしかは2000年にアメリカで「排除された」とされていた感染症です。生後6週間の赤ちゃんはMMRワクチンを接種できる月齢に達していない。ここで笑うところはないし、笑うつもりもない。ただ、事実として書いておきたかった。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> 検死官が死因を確認した。保健長官はその種の情報を信じないと決めていた。

---

## 5. Trump Will Fly to Ireland on Qatar's Gifted Jet — Security Questions Unresolved

*The Guardian US（[記事](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/04/trump-qatar-jet-ireland)）*

トランプ大統領が来週のアイルランド訪問に、カタールから贈与された航空機を使用する予定であることが明らかになった。7月の使用時にはイランの脅威情報が発覚し、大統領が別機に移送されるという事態が起きていた。

**どこが笑える？**

トランプ大統領が来週のアイルランド訪問に、カタールから贈られたボーイングを使う予定だ。この飛行機、7月にイランの脅威情報が発覚して、大統領が急きょ別機に移された、あの飛行機です。セキュリティ上の問題は今も未解決、と報道されている。出発は来週。

「前回は問題があったけど今回は大丈夫」という判断の根拠が何なのか、記事を読んでも分からなかった。もしかしたら根拠はないのかもしれない。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> 7月にこの飛行機から降ろされた。9月の解決策：ヨーロッパへ飛ぶ。

---

## 今日のまとめジョーク/パンチライン

> 今週のアメリカ、自国の中央銀行を脅して、刑務所でFDA未承認品を売って、ソ連生まれのパズルゲームをパクって、検死官の報告を否定して、7月に降ろされた飛行機をもう一回飛ばそうとしています。ルールは気分らしい。

今日も読んでくれてありがとうございます。また明日の朝、ここで。
